subject: Radiological Signs
title: Classic Chest X-Ray (CXR) Signs
preview: Recognize major chest radiograph patterns while remembering that classic X-ray signs are neither universally present nor diagnostic alone.

sections.title: Pneumothorax and collapse
points: Deep sulcus: abnormally deep lateral costophrenic angle on supine chest imaging in some pneumothoraces.
Golden S sign: S-shaped displaced fissure associated with an upper-lobe collapse pattern and possible central mass.

sections.title: Pulmonary vascular clues
points: Hampton hump: peripheral pleural-based wedge opacity can reflect pulmonary infarction.
Westermark sign: focal oligemia may follow pulmonary artery obstruction, but is rarely sufficient for diagnosis.

sections.title: A large cardiac silhouette
points: A globular “water bottle” cardiac silhouette may accompany a large pericardial effusion.
Echocardiography assesses pericardial fluid and physiology when clinically indicated.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: A normal chest radiograph does not exclude pulmonary embolism.
A silhouette sign may have several causes; interpret with the clinical picture and appropriate imaging.

quickRevision: A deep sulcus on a supine radiograph can suggest pneumothorax.
A Golden S sign can arise from lobar collapse associated with a central obstructing lesion.
Hampton hump and Westermark sign are historical clues to pulmonary embolism but are insensitive.

quiz.question: What does an air bronchogram suggest on chest radiography?
options: Free air outside the lung only
Calcification of the entire bronchial tree
Air-filled bronchi outlined by air-space opacity
quiz.explanation: An air bronchogram occurs when air-filled bronchi remain visible against surrounding air-space opacification, as in certain consolidative lung processes.
